title: Deferred Decode Controller: kernel affinity matrix, attention-window rewrite, and confidence-hinge fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a 'Deferred Decode Controller' (DDC) that schedules prefill and decode work using a kernel affinity matrix and an attention-window rewriter, and makes go/no-go decisions using a new confidence-hinge acceptance metric. The DDC sits between the request router and the kernel scheduler and coordinates: 1) mapping model variants and sequence-length profiles to preferred kernels (kernel affinity matrix); 2) rewriting prefill KV plans to avoid redundant attention spans when inputs are short or dominated by system tokens (attention-window rewrite); 3) evaluating a lightweight, fast-to-compute 'confidence-hinge' score early in decode to decide whether to continue the optimistic fast-path or immediately pivot to a more robust but costlier execution path. This ticket covers design, prototype runtime hooks, telemetry, and an automated rollback/fallback policy to ensure graceful degradation under miscalibration.
acceptance_criteria: DDC prototypes scheduling API and integrates with existing router and kernel-selector hooks in a canary runtime build.

Kernel affinity matrix produced for three representative model+hw combinations and validated by synthetic workload: throughput improvement >= 8% on short-sequence workloads without increasing 95th-percentile latency by >5%.
Attention-window rewriter reduces average KV prefill tokens by >= 12% on internal conversational prompt corpus without degrading Rouge/BLEU-style quality metrics for targeted prompt sets.
Confidence-hinge acceptance metric evaluated on 100k historical requests: true-positive acceptance (fast-path kept and output matches full-decode) >= 94% at operating point, false-accept rate < 6%.

Fallback path (rollforward to conservative kernels/fully-qualified decode) triggers automatically on acceptance-hinge failure and maintains overall correctness while bounding cost increase to < 30% for failed fast-pathes.
Telemetry dashboard updated: per-route hinge scores, kernel-affinity transitions, prefill token savings, and rollback frequency visible in Console rollout view.
Runbook with rollback steps and incident checklist reviewed and approved by SRE and runtime leads.
implementation_steps: Design DDC API contract: scheduling hooks, kernel-affinity table format, and hinge score schema (week 1).
Instrument small in-memory kernel-affinity producer that consumes hot-path metrics and outputs static affinity tables for canary models (week 2).
Implement attention-window rewriter as a prefill planner transform that can be toggled per-route; include unit tests for common prompt shapes (week 2-3).
Prototype confidence-hinge: lightweight token-level heuristic + small model-free scoring function; integrate with DDC decision path (week 3).
Add fallback plumbing: fast-path abort signals, KV cache reconciliation, and graceful rollforward to conservative path with telemetry emitters (week 4).
Canary deployment: 1% of traffic for two routes, collect hinge confusion matrix and perf metrics; iterate thresholds (week 5).
Dashboard and alerts: hinge drift alert, rollback rate SLI, and cost-per-token shift. Document runbook and SRE handoff (week 6).
risks: Hinge miscalibration could cause silent quality regressions if fallback is not triggered quickly enough.
Affinity matrix staleness: model architecture changes or kernel upgrades may invalidate mappings and degrade perf.
Attention-window rewrite could inadvertently remove context needed by some prompt patterns leading to subtle regressions on long-tail prompts.
Increased complexity in scheduler may interact poorly with existing autoscaling heuristics and queue backpressure.
